name: Blueberry Cinnamon Oatmeal
flavorProfile: Creamy coconut-milk oatmeal sweetened with maple, topped with warm blueberries and a hit of cinnamon.
healthBenefit: Oats simmered in coconut milk and water, with warm blueberries, cinnamon, maple and a little vanilla stirred through, a whole-food breakfast that is also soy-free.
instructions: Combine the oats, cinnamon, salt, coconut milk and water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Fold in the blueberries and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, just until they soften.
Stir in the maple syrup and vanilla and serve warm.

name: Strawberry Banana Oatmeal
flavorProfile: Coconut-milk oatmeal with sliced banana stirred in and fresh strawberries piled on top.
healthBenefit: A simple, classic pairing built on the same clean oats-and-coconut-milk base, with whole fruit doing all the sweetening work.
instructions: Combine the oats, coconut milk, water, cinnamon and salt in a small saucepan and bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat down to a simmer.
Cook, stirring now and then, for 5-7 minutes, until thick and creamy. Add a splash more water if it gets too thick.
Stir in half the banana slices during the last minute so they warm through.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the remaining banana, the strawberries and the maple syrup if using.

name: Baked Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Cup
flavorProfile: A single-serving baked oatmeal cup with diced apple, walnuts and cinnamon, sweet enough from the apple that the maple syrup is optional.
healthBenefit: Baking the oats concentrates the apple's natural sweetness, so the maple syrup can be left out, and the whole dish is built from a short, whole-food ingredient list.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350F (175C) and grease a small oven-safe ramekin or cup.
Stir the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt together in the ramekin.
Stir in the coconut milk, maple syrup if using, and vanilla, then fold in the diced apple and walnuts.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until set and lightly golden on top.
Let cool for a couple of minutes before eating.

name: Date & Cinnamon Overnight Oats
flavorProfile: No-cook overnight oats soaked in coconut milk, sweetened only by chopped dates and cinnamon.
healthBenefit: A real make-ahead option built on the same clean base as this batch's other oat dishes, ready to eat straight from the fridge.
instructions: Combine the oats, coconut milk, chopped dates, cinnamon and the pinch of salt in a jar or container.
Stir well, cover, and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
Stir again before eating; add a splash more coconut milk if you prefer it looser.

name: Orange Cranberry Rice Pudding
flavorProfile: Brown rice simmered slowly in coconut milk until creamy, finished with fresh orange segments and cranberries.
healthBenefit: A rice pudding, built entirely on clean, whole-food ingredients, with orange and cranberry's natural tartness balancing the coconut milk's richness.
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, maple syrup, cinnamon and the pinch of salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring often, for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the rice is fully tender and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Stir in the cranberries for the last 5 minutes so they soften and release some colour.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the vanilla, and top with the orange segments just before serving, warm or chilled.

name: Ginger Pear Rice Pudding
flavorProfile: Creamy coconut-milk rice pudding with fresh ginger and warm cinnamon, topped with sliced pear.
healthBenefit: Fresh ginger gives this rice pudding real warmth without needing any of the spices flagged for Hashimoto's in this app's reference database.
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, grated ginger, cinnamon, maple syrup and the pinch of salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring often, for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the rice is fully tender and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the vanilla, and top with the sliced pear just before serving, warm or chilled.

name: Peach Sorghum Porridge
flavorProfile: Whole-grain sorghum simmered in coconut milk with cinnamon, ginger and vanilla, finished with chia and topped with sliced peach and almonds.
healthBenefit: Sorghum is a different whole grain from oats or rice, and one of the few this database scores completely clean for Hashimoto's.
instructions: Rinse the sorghum, then combine it in a saucepan with the coconut milk, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and maple syrup and bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover and cook for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the sorghum is tender. You can also cook everything in a greased slow cooker on low for about 8 hours, as the source does.
Take off the heat, stir in the chia seeds and let it stand 5 to 10 minutes to thicken.
Top with the sliced peach and the sliced almonds.

name: Raspberry Lime Sorghum Porridge
flavorProfile: Creamy sorghum porridge finished with fresh raspberries and a bright squeeze of lime.
healthBenefit: A genuinely different flavor direction from this batch's other porridges, real citrus brightening a rich, whole-grain base.

ingredients.prepNote: juice of a quarter of a lime

instructions: Rinse the sorghum, then combine it in a saucepan with the coconut milk, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and maple syrup and bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover and cook for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the sorghum is tender. You can also cook everything in a greased slow cooker on low for about 8 hours, as the source does.
Take off the heat, stir in the chia seeds and lime juice and let it stand 5 to 10 minutes to thicken.
Top with the raspberries and the sliced almonds.

name: Sweet Polenta with Warm Apricot Compote
flavorProfile: Creamy coconut-milk polenta topped with apricots stewed soft with cinnamon.
healthBenefit: Cornmeal polenta cooked in coconut milk makes a different sweet breakfast base from any grain elsewhere in this batch.
instructions: Bring the coconut milk and 60ml water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, then whisk in the cornmeal a little at a time so no lumps form.
Cook for 8-10 minutes over low heat, whisking often, until thick and smooth. Add a splash of water if it gets too stiff.
Meanwhile, put the apricot, lemon juice, cinnamon and 1 tablespoon water in a small pan, cover and stew over low heat for 5-8 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Spoon the warm apricot compote over the polenta and drizzle with the maple syrup if using.

name: Banana Polenta Porridge
flavorProfile: Smooth coconut-milk polenta topped with sliced banana, warm maple syrup and a dusting of cinnamon.
healthBenefit: A different texture from oatmeal or rice pudding, with sliced banana and warm maple syrup on top.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 teaspoon cooked in, the rest warmed and drizzled on top

instructions: Whisk the cornmeal slowly into the water, coconut milk, 1 teaspoon of the maple syrup, the salt and the vanilla in a small pot.
Bring to a boil over medium high heat, whisking often, then lower to a simmer and keep whisking for about 10 minutes, until it starts to thicken.
Switch to a spoon and simmer gently for about 20 minutes more, scraping the bottom and sides often, until smooth and soft.
Just before it is done, slice the banana and warm the rest of the maple syrup.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the banana, the warm maple syrup and a dusting of cinnamon, and serve warm.

name: Pineapple Coconut Tapioca Pudding
flavorProfile: Small tapioca pearls simmered slowly in coconut milk until glossy and thick, topped with fresh pineapple.
healthBenefit: A different texture from a porridge or rice pudding, tapioca pearls soaked and then cooked low and slow in coconut milk, with no other liquid.
instructions: Soak the tapioca pearls in about a third of the coconut milk for 1 hour.
Pour the pearls and any liquid left into a saucepan with the rest of the coconut milk, the maple syrup, vanilla and salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pearls turn translucent and the pudding thickens.
Let cool for about 10 minutes to eat warm, or chill overnight. Top with the diced pineapple before eating.

name: Mixed Berry Coconut Tapioca Pudding
flavorProfile: Coconut-milk tapioca pudding topped with fresh blackberries and raspberries.
healthBenefit: The same clean tapioca-and-coconut-milk base as this batch's pineapple version, with a genuinely different, tart-berry finish.
instructions: Soak the tapioca pearls in about a third of the coconut milk for 1 hour.
Pour the pearls and any liquid left into a saucepan with the rest of the coconut milk, the maple syrup, vanilla and salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pearls turn translucent and the pudding thickens.
Let cool for about 10 minutes to eat warm, or chill overnight. Top with the blackberries and raspberries before eating.

name: Tropical Fruit Bowl with Coconut
flavorProfile: A no-cook bowl of banana, pineapple, papaya, and orange, drizzled with a little coconut milk.
healthBenefit: A genuinely raw, no-cook option built entirely from real whole fruit, ready in minutes with nothing to simmer.
instructions: Slice or dice all the fruit and combine it in a bowl.
Squeeze the lime juice over and toss gently, so the banana stays bright.
Drizzle the coconut milk over the top just before serving.

name: Citrus Avocado Breakfast Bowl
flavorProfile: Diced avocado with rounds of orange and grapefruit in a lime and vinegar dressing, with fresh mint.
healthBenefit: A savory-leaning, no-cook breakfast built on whole avocado as its one fat source, with citrus rounds in a sharp lime and vinegar dressing.
instructions: Whisk the lime juice and vinegar in the bottom of a shallow bowl and season with most of the salt and the pepper.
Cut the peel and white pith off the orange and grapefruit, following the curve of the fruit, then slice them into thin rounds, pick out any seeds, and toss them in the dressing.
Dice the avocado and fold it in gently. Scatter the mint leaves and the last of the salt over the top and eat right away.

name: Berry Banana Coconut Smoothie
flavorProfile: A thick, no-cook smoothie of banana, blueberry, and strawberry blended with coconut milk, a little maple and a pinch of cinnamon.
healthBenefit: A quick option for a busy morning, built entirely from this batch's clean fruit-and-coconut-milk palette.
instructions: Put the banana, blueberries, strawberries, coconut milk, water, maple syrup and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend for about 30 seconds, until smooth.
Add a few ice cubes if you like it colder, pour into a glass and drink right away.

name: Savory Rice Bowl with Zucchini, Pepper & Tomato
flavorProfile: Simmered rice topped with zucchini, bell pepper, and tomato cooked soft in a splash of water, finished with fresh cilantro and lime.
healthBenefit: A genuinely savory option built without any oil at all, since every real cooking oil in this app's reference database is flagged for Hashimoto's -- the vegetables are cooked in a splash of water instead, a real, workable technique, not a compromise.
instructions: Combine the rice and filtered water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30-35 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, cook the zucchini and bell pepper in a tablespoon of water in a covered pan over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, until soft, adding a little more water if the pan gets dry.
Stir in the diced tomato and cook 1-2 minutes more, just until warmed through.
Mix the hot rice with the cilantro, lime juice, lemon juice and salt, and spoon the vegetables over it.

name: Savory Polenta with Leeks & Tomato
flavorProfile: Smooth water-based polenta topped with leeks and tomato cooked soft, finished with fresh cilantro and lime.
healthBenefit: A different savory grain base from the rice bowl in this same batch, still built entirely without any pressed oil.
instructions: Cook the sliced leek in a tablespoon of the water in a covered saucepan over medium heat for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft. Spoon it out and set aside.
Bring the rest of the water to a boil in the same pan and slowly whisk in the cornmeal.
Lower the heat and stir often for 15-20 minutes until thick and creamy, adding the salt a little at a time.
Stir the diced tomato into the leek and warm it through for 1-2 minutes.
Spoon the leek and tomato over the polenta and finish with the pepper, cilantro and lime juice.

name: Zucchini & Fennel Breakfast Hash with Avocado
flavorProfile: Zucchini and fennel cooked soft with tomato, topped with sliced avocado, cilantro, and lime.
healthBenefit: A different vegetable combination from this batch's other savory dishes, with sliced avocado standing in for the richness a pressed oil would normally add.

ingredients.prepNote: juice of a quarter of a lime

instructions: Cook the zucchini and fennel in a splash of water in a covered pan over medium heat for 7-9 minutes, until soft, adding a little more water if the pan gets dry.
Uncover, add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato and cook 1-2 minutes more, just until warmed through, then season with the salt and pepper.
Transfer to a plate and top with the avocado, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

name: Cranberry Orange Oatmeal
flavorProfile: Coconut-milk oatmeal finished with fresh cranberries and orange segments.
healthBenefit: Cranberry's tartness against orange's sweetness gives this oatmeal a different flavor from this batch's other fruit pairings.
instructions: Combine the oats, cinnamon, salt, coconut milk and water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy, stirring in the cranberries for the last 2 minutes so they soften.
Stir in the maple syrup and vanilla, top with the orange segments, and serve warm.

name: Papaya Lime Smoothie Bowl
flavorProfile: A thick, no-cook smoothie bowl of papaya and banana blended with coconut milk and fresh lime.
healthBenefit: A genuinely different fruit base from this batch's berry-forward smoothie, ready in minutes with nothing to cook.
instructions: Put the frozen papaya and banana, the carrot juice, coconut milk, lime juice, ginger and the agave syrup if using in a blender.
Blend until creamy and smooth, adding a splash more carrot juice or coconut milk only if the blender struggles, so the bowl stays thick.
Taste and add more lime or ginger if you like, then spoon into a bowl and eat right away.

name: Cantaloupe & Grapefruit Breakfast Bowl
flavorProfile: A no-cook bowl of fresh cantaloupe and grapefruit with a squeeze of lime.
healthBenefit: A light, refreshing option built from whole fruit, with no grain or coconut milk at all.

ingredients.prepNote: zest grated and juice squeezed, from a quarter of a lime

instructions: Stir the sugar, minced mint and grated lime zest together in a small bowl. Make it no more than an hour before eating so the zest stays fragrant.
Combine the diced cantaloupe and grapefruit segments in a bowl and drizzle with the lime juice, stirring gently to coat.
Sprinkle the lime mint sugar over the fruit, turn it once or twice to coat, and eat right away.

name: Apple Rice Pudding with Cinnamon
flavorProfile: Creamy coconut-milk rice pudding with diced apple and cinnamon stirred through.
healthBenefit: A genuinely different fruit pairing from this batch's other rice puddings, apple and cinnamon a classic, simple combination.
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, maple syrup and the pinch of salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.

Cook uncovered, stirring often, for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the rice is fully tender and the mixture is thick and creamy. Stir in the apple and cinnamon for the last 10 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the vanilla, and serve warm or chilled.

name: Date Sorghum Porridge
flavorProfile: Whole-grain sorghum simmered in coconut milk with chopped dates and cinnamon.
healthBenefit: A genuinely different sweetener direction from this batch's other sorghum porridge, real dates doing most of the sweetening.
instructions: Rinse the sorghum, then combine it in a saucepan with the coconut milk, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and maple syrup and bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover and cook for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the sorghum is tender. You can also cook everything in a greased slow cooker on low for about 8 hours, as the source does.
Stir in the chopped dates for the last 5 minutes so they soften.
Take off the heat, stir in the chia seeds and let it stand 5 to 10 minutes to thicken. Top with the sliced almonds.

name: Savory Fennel & Tomato Rice Bowl
flavorProfile: Simmered rice topped with fennel and tomato cooked soft in a splash of water, finished with fresh cilantro and lime.
healthBenefit: A different savory vegetable pairing from this batch's other rice bowl, still built entirely without any pressed oil.
instructions: Combine the rice and filtered water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30-35 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, cook the fennel in a tablespoon of water in a covered pan over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, until soft, adding a little more water if the pan gets dry.
Stir in the diced tomato and cook 1-2 minutes more, just until warmed through.
Mix the hot rice with the cilantro, lime juice, lemon juice and salt, and spoon the vegetables over it.

name: Pear Ginger Overnight Oats
flavorProfile: No-cook overnight oats soaked in coconut milk with fresh ginger and diced pear.
healthBenefit: A genuinely different overnight-oats flavor from this batch's date-and-cinnamon version, fresh ginger giving it real warmth without needing any of the spices flagged for Hashimoto's in this app's reference database.
instructions: Combine the oats, coconut milk, diced pear, grated ginger and the pinch of salt in a jar or container.
Stir well, cover, and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
Stir again before eating; add a splash more coconut milk if you prefer it looser.

name: Blackberry Lime Rice Pudding
flavorProfile: Creamy coconut-milk rice pudding topped with fresh blackberries and a squeeze of lime.
healthBenefit: A different berry pairing from this batch's other rice puddings, lime brightening the blackberries' natural tartness.

ingredients.prepNote: juice of a quarter of a lime

instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, maple syrup, cinnamon and the pinch of salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring often, for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick, until the rice is fully tender and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vanilla and lime juice. Top with the blackberries and serve warm or chilled.
